summary: Josef Schick worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied under Albrecht Weber, at the University of Tübingen (~1878-1882), and earned a PhD from Humboldt University of Berlin (1887-1889), later holding posts at Berlin, Bonn, Heidelberg, and Munich (1896-1925).

Josef Strzygowski was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Munich (~1884-1887). He taught Ernst Gombrich and Stella Kramrisch, and held posts at the University of Graz (~1892-1909), the University of Vienna (~1909-1933), and Åbo Akademi University.
Josef van Ess was a scholar in religious studies and related fields. He studied at the University of Bonn (~1954-1959) and later held a post at the University of Tübingen (~1968-1999).

Joseph Campbell worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Canterbury School, Dartmouth College, Columbia University (BA 1925, master's ~1925-1927), and the universities of Paris and Munich. He taught at Canterbury School (1933) and Sarah Lawrence College (1934-1972).
Joseph D. Markowski is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a Master of Arts at McGill University, where he studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2004).

Joseph E. Schwartzberg worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Brooklyn College, University of Maryland, University of Paris, and Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hartshorne (PhD 1960). He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, JNU, and University of Minnesota (1964-2000).

Joseph Estlin Carpenter was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at University College School (~1856-1860) and the University of London (~1860-1866), later serving at Harris Manchester College (~1876-1915) and the University of Oxford (~1906-1915).

Joseph Goldstein is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Columbia University (~1961-1965) and trained under numerous teachers including Anagarika Munindra. He taught at Naropa University in 1974 and co-founded the Insight Meditation Society and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Joseph Hackin worked in history/archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot, earned a doctorate from the University of Paris, and held posts at the Musée Guimet, École du Louvre, and DAFA.

Joseph Haroutunian was a religious studies scholar who studied at the American University of Beirut, Columbia University (PhD ~1930-1932), and Union Theological Seminary. He held teaching posts at Wellesley College (1932-1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940-1962), and the University of Chicago (1962-1968).

Joseph Kitagawa was a religious studies, Japanology, and history scholar. He studied at Rikkyo University, CDSP, Seabury-Western, and Chicago under Joachim Wach (PhD ~1951). He spent his career at the University of Chicago (1951-1987), serving as dean of the Divinity School.

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst College, Harvard University, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He founded the Nalanda Institute and served as a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Joseph A. Marino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2017) under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, and held a post as assistant professor at the same university (attested 2026).

Joseph Needham was a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. He was educated at Oundle School, Gonville and Caius College, and the University of Cambridge (~1918-1925), later holding posts at Cambridge (~1924-1966), Gonville and Caius, and the Needham Research Institute (~1987-1990).

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under Bernard Williams. He held posts at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and held visiting professorships at United Theological College, UC Santa Barbara, and the Ecumenical Institute of Bossey.

Joseph Ratzinger was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich (~1947-1951) and Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at the universities of Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen (~1966-1969), and Regensburg (~1969-1977).

Joseph Rock was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He held positions at Mills College (~1908), Mid-Pacific Institute, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908-1920), the United States Department of Agriculture (~1920-1924), and the Army Map Service (1944).

Joseph Tiefenthaler was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held a post as rector at St. Peter's College, Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and history/archaeology who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1824-1858), INALCO (1838), and as president of the Société Asiatique (1847, 1852).

Joseph Vendryes was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901-1960), University of Paris (~1907-1946), and École Normale Supérieure (~1920-1946).
